answers.answer: They cannot win as Usurper during the Act in which they take the title. Their next Wake checks for victory before flipping the title; at that check they are not yet Usurper. They can first win at the following Wake, provided they still hold the title, or at the end of round 8 if that arrives first while they remain Usurper. If they lose the title, they cannot win; retaking it resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts this sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘at the start of an Exile's turn during Wake, or at the end of round 8’; the sequence after taking the title is ‘next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake’; ‘Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper.’

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary win also requires the Exile to have the true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and have at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck. For Conquest and Sanctuary, ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player, so a tie does not count.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions table lists the four Oath–Vision pairs; Visionary victory requires ‘at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck’; Conquest/Sanctuary require ‘strictly more than every other player, no ties.’

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. A Citizen who meets the Successor goal wins alone instead of the Chancellor when the roll ends the game. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll.
answers.evidence: Stable regime: ‘at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll end die only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper’; the listed ending results are 6 / 5–6 / 3–6; ‘An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.’

answers.answer: At the end of round 8, check in this order: (1) if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper, the Empire wins; the Chancellor wins unless a Citizen qualifies as Successor, in which case that Citizen wins alone; (2) otherwise, an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise, a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest, then Rebellion, then Sanctuary, then Faith; (4) otherwise the Empire wins, again with a qualified Citizen Successor replacing the Chancellor. Thus holding a Successor goal does not independently end the game; it replaces a Chancellor win.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion lists the four checks in this exact priority and states that Citizen Successor replaces any Chancellor win; ‘Holding Successor goal never ends game on its own.’

answers.answer: Supremacy: hold more relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold the Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold the Grand Scepter. Citizens and the Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or as Usurper.
answers.evidence: Oath table gives each ‘Citizen Successor goal’; Visionary victory says ‘Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.’

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, either place 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank, choosing among tied banks. Never remove its last favor: if it has 1, add 1 if able; if you have none, do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After these choices, check whether it has at least 6 favor and flip it to Mob if so. Becoming Mob at that final check does not trigger a second payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake, step 1: either add or return favor; ‘Never remove its last favor’; Mob-side repeats the choice once; ‘Afterwards, if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob’; becoming Mob then ‘does not retroactively repeat the payment that Wake.’

answers.answer: Rest order: return favor on denizens and edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens, edifices, and relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply (Exiles and Chancellor by remaining personal-bank warbands, Citizens to the exact Chancellor marker space); save unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent point, capped at the leftmost space (7 Supply); then optionally use Rest powers, each once, in chosen order. Citizen refresh copies the Chancellor marker exactly, including the leftmost space, rather than counting purple warbands.
answers.evidence: Rest: mandatory order steps 1–5; step 3 says Citizen refreshes to the ‘exact Chancellor marker space’; step 4 saves remaining Supply by moving left, capped at leftmost (7 Supply).

answers.answer: Search uses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn's region, never both. A regional discard Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 Supply at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces that world-deck cost with 2, with other applicable modifiers still applying. Draw 3 unless the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces the draw; you cannot voluntarily stop early. From the world deck draw one card at a time: a Vision is announced, stops Search immediately, and advances Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop Search or advance the track. If the source runs out, draw only what remains; no reshuffle is implied.
answers.evidence: Search section gives source and costs, says draw 3 and ‘cannot voluntarily stop early’; world-deck Vision ‘stop immediately’ and advances track, while discard-pile Visions do neither.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's discard pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; order multiple discards as you choose. Cards from hand or advisers use your pawn's region. If discarding a card located at a site in another region, use that card's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets on it go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Discard destinations section specifies the region cycle, uses the pawn's region for hand/advisers and the card's region for a remote site card; favor returns immediately and secrets go facedown to the actor's board.

answers.answer: You may have up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser subject to locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, check against the new limit before playing it, using the lowest of multiple limits. Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner, or power; any card, including a site-only card or Vision, can be held facedown. Later, as a minor action, a facedown adviser may be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when another rule permits or requires it. A true Vision played faceup by an Exile occupies the separate Revealed Vision slot, not an adviser slot; it replaces and discards the old revealed Vision. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search adviser options describe the 3-card limit, facedown properties and later minor-action options; True Vision option says it occupies a separate Exile slot and replaces the prior Vision.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply: place 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site, then gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board (purple for a Citizen). It does not require ruling the site; relics and ruins are ineligible, and it is not remote. Trade costs 1 Supply and also uses an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site. Either put 1 secret on the card to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank, or put 2 favor on the card to gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers do not match; if none match, the second option gives zero secrets. Resource exhaustion limits gains to what is available; secrets are unlimited. Costs remain payable even if a gain is reduced to zero.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections specify costs, eligible cards, gains, destinations, matching faceup advisers, and the zero-secret result with no matches.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. A banner can be recovered from anywhere, including another player, yourself, or the shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than is on it, put the payment on the banner, distribute the old favor one at a time among suit banks in printed order beginning at a bank you choose, and flip it to normal side if Mob. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds, put the payment on it; the new holder takes 1 old secret and the previous holder takes the rest. If recovering it from yourself, all old secrets return to you; from the shared bank, the remainder stays there. Recovering a banner has no seizure penalty.
answers.evidence: Recover section lists relic target/cost and separate People's Favor/Darkest Secret recovery procedures, including distribution of old resources and no seizure penalty.

answers.answer: Another player's Darkest Secret is recoverable only if a suited card at their pawn's site matches none of their faceup advisers. A site with no cards, or only a ruin, protects it. If the holder has no faceup advisers but there is a suited site card, it is recoverable because that card matches none of the adviser's suits. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. The protection does not apply when recovering the Secret from yourself or the shared bank.
answers.evidence: Corrected Darkest Secret protection: requires a suited card at their pawn's site matching none of their faceup advisers; empty and ruin-only sites protect it; with zero faceup advisers a suited site card is recoverable.

answers.answer: Choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may add any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map, each adding 1 defense die. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics, banners, or their pawn together with their favor; these targets use their printed defense dice, banner dice equal to resources on the banner, or 2 dice for pawn-and-favor. A co-located defender's relic target alone satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2 give defender eligibility, the local-target rule, remote-site targeting, co-located relic/banner/pawn targets, and the relic exception to the local-target requirement.

answers.answer: The attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in their board force; relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonuses apply. Defense is shields rolled, with each double-symbol doubling shields and multipliers stacking, plus all defending warbands at targeted sites and the defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only. Bandits add 1 defense per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills 1 of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords, then add 1 attack for each pair of hollow swords; an unmatched hollow sword adds zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing, must sacrifice exactly enough to win and cannot sacrifice excess. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie is a defender win.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4, and 5 specify dice pools, defense calculation, skull casualties, sword/hollow-sword scoring, exact-enough sacrifice, and strict victory threshold.

answers.answer: Resolve defeat first: the defeated side kills half its remaining force, rounded down, and returns survivors to board; bandits cannot be killed and hide. If Imperial defenders are defeated, the Chancellor chooses which defending warbands die; surviving site warbands go to the Chancellor's board, while surviving Citizens' board warbands stay on those boards. If the attacker won, they may place any number of surviving force warbands, including zero, on any targeted sites. Zero leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. They take all targeted relics and banners. A seized banner taken by any method other than Recover loses 2 resources, to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site without Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker's destination choice if its enemy ruler chooses. Then finish battle-plan effects: defeated effects after casualties, attacker target/banishment effects, victorious effects, and finally ‘At end, discard’ instructions; all are part of the Campaign. Transfer Supremacy at Campaign end, not at temporary loss of site rule.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8 cover defeat, optional zero garrisons, target capture, banner penalty, banishment/favor, Shrouded Wood, and battle-plan resolution order.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. Relevant modifiers from the defender and Allies apply, and the title defense bonus is shared on the defending side even outside Supremacy. Allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. Defenders/Allies may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not another player's advisers; the user pays and a plan can only be used once. The declared defender chooses order, timing, priority, and shared-plan user if Allies disagree. The Chancellor chooses Imperial defending casualties; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board and surviving Citizen board warbands remain there. In a Campaign by a Citizen against the Chancellor or another Citizen, that Citizen attacker is non-Imperial; when the Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen defender is non-Imperial for that Campaign. This does not make every Citizen non-Imperial for an intra-Empire battle.
answers.evidence: Imperial defense bullets specify Chancellor's automatic alliance, Citizen allies, modifiers/warbands/plans, defender priority and casualties; Campaign step 1 states which Citizen becomes non-Imperial in the specified attacks.

answers.answer: Base Travel Supply costs by origin→destination region are: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, Cradle 2, Provinces 2, Hinterland 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. Revealing a facedown destination places its printed favor and secrets there from the shared bank and its printed number of relics facedown beside it from the relic deck. Apply the fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. Free Travel is the final override: any applicable ‘spend no Supply’ power makes payment zero even if another power increases cost. Entry restrictions still apply unless expressly ignored. The summary gives these interaction rules but does not specify a general numeric formula for every possible fixed-cost modifier combination.
answers.evidence: Travel section provides the region cost table and reveal effects; it states ‘fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases’ and ‘Free Travel is the final override.’

answers.answer: During play, only the Grand Scepter holder can offer Citizenship, and not on the turn they took the Scepter. In a later turn, the holder may offer any Exile, including themself, and must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; they may also negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and may let the recipient peek at Reliquary relics. Other binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics. Acceptance turns the Exile into a Citizen, replaces their own warbands on board and map with purple (if insufficient purple, the new Citizen chooses which to remove and replace), discards their revealed Vision, flips their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if accepted during their own turn, refreshes them to full Supply, exchanges the promised pieces, and gives the Chancellor the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers apply acceptance without a negotiated offer.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play: Offer and Acceptance paragraphs specify timing, required Reliquary relic and optional binding exchange, plus all acceptance effects.

answers.answer: If the winner won by Vision alone, the next Oath matches that Vision. For any other victory or multiple victory methods, the winner chooses any Oath except the current one, and the goal is saved in the World Box. If an Exile won, flip all Citizen boards, including boxed ones, to Exile. The winner may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; Chronicle offers have no normal in-play offer requirements. Each accepting Exile must flip their board to Citizen and replace every garrison at every site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site, regardless of the old garrison size; the winner cannot offer themself. Rebuild the world deck by shuffling remaining in-play denizens (excluding those retained at sites, in Archive, or Dispossessed), making a top stack of 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards), a middle stack of 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), and the remaining denizens below. The top stack is 12 cards, not 14: the Chronicle aid's printed ‘12 denizens + 2’ is incorrect.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle: steps 1, 2, and 9 give the Oath rule, Citizenship turnover, and deck stacks; step 9 explicitly corrects the aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ and says the top stack is 10 denizens + 2 Visions.
